titre: TRIADE: Enabling LLM Agents to Write Native Code by Hand Under Signed-Intent Governance (Academic Edition v0.19.0) — manuscript, data tables, complete sources and verification evidence
description: The academic edition v0.19.0 of the TRIADE single-case study: a development protocol under which an LLM agent writes native x86-64, RISC-V and TLS 1.3 code directly as assembly notation, governed by signed layer-I specifications. This edition carries the closure of the D210 extension campaign: four further units at identical formats across arms and randomized arm order (the pre-registered plan, hash consigned before any measurement), the fourth unit closed on its red at the delivery cap with three counted escapes all kit-side in the shared judge (the piece never at fault at either format), and the empirical attribution — the same C piece re-delivered through a minimal standard kit — reading 14 VERT, 0 ROUGE: the compiled pure flow would not have produced the escapes. The hypotheses close explicit: H6 holds by attribution, H7 untested on a draw that gave no contrast (carried to the next campaign), H8 falsified as the corrective spiral declined (51%/39%/9%; the first unit 44%, the couture named). This deposit contains the manuscript (30 pages), the consolidated data tables (the RQ2 instrumented round-trip measurements, the D204 and D210 campaign ledgers, the carnet M3 as filed, the exact-trace constant-time replays, the M4 optimization measurements), the complete edition sources, the TLA+ models with the coverage lemma, the generative conformance campaign evidence, the D210 reception reports, and the ten-point verification report.
